item.title: Danish actor nominated for French equivalent of Oscar
item.description: Danish actor Claes Bang has been nominated for a César, France’s equivalent of an Oscar, for his role in “Den nye triumfbue”. This historical drama, also featuring Sidse Babett Knudsen, has been nominated in seven other categories, including Best Director for Stéphane Demoustier. item.title: Macron to bolster Arctic defense due to China, Russia
item.description: French President Emmanuel Macron emphasizes a strengthened defense in the Arctic due to the actions of Russia and China’s economic presence. item.title: Schools get more funding when students take part of vocational training abroad
item.description: From January, Danish vocational schools will get higher funding for students and apprentices who complete part of their training abroad. The increased support applies to students without a Danish training agreement and helps schools arrange paid training in foreign companies.

item.title: Denmark’s young and international workers struggle with unpaid internships
item.description: Despite tens of thousands of placements each year, unpaid and short-term internships leave job seekers frustrated, exploited, and struggling to find long-term work, with international students and non-EU residents facing the greatest hurdles.

item.title: Lego used as therapy for Ukrainian refugee kids in Lithuania
item.description: Lego bricks are used in Lithuania to help Ukrainian children who fled Ukraine and now reside in the country. This initiative is part of the collaboration between Vytautas Magnus University and a Ukrainian center in Vilnius. item.title: Norwegian oil fund worth nearly 14 trillion kroner
item.description: By the end of 2025, the Norwegian oil fund was valued at 21,000 billion Norwegian kroner (approximately 14,000 billion Danish kroner). A year prior, its value was 19,700 billion Norwegian kroner. Key investments include 574 billion in Nvidia, 497 billion in Apple, and 459 billion in Microsoft. item.description: Officials from Denmark, the USA, and Greenland began meetings on Wednesday to reduce tensions around the Arctic.
